title: Reuse binary TensorView label lookup for selectors
finding: TensorView construction already used binary lookup over canonical sorted TensorAxis.labels after G1-TENSOR-01BG, but selector validation still used Python membership against the full label tuple. That left one high-cardinality path performing a linear axis-label scan and duplicated the exact-label membership rule beside construction validation.
primary_claim: TensorView now routes construction and selector label membership through one small module-local exact binary lookup helper over the already canonical sorted axis labels. Selector validation no longer performs a full label membership scan. Fourfold/Forest source identity, tensor status, provenance, duplicate-claim refusal, canonical ordering and public wire contracts remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Factor only the existing exact bisect membership rule into one module-local helper and reuse it for selector validation. Do not add an axis index cache, lookup service, alternate TensorAxis type, planner, store, registry or backend abstraction for a sorted tuple that already supports logarithmic lookup.
acceptance: TensorView selector validation does not linearly scan canonical axis labels merely to establish exact membership
construction validation and selector validation share one exact sorted-label membership rule
